moves.note: OPEN with named gap: the only ending found is a general statute (49 Stat. 375) that does not name the order; recorded as a candidate.
All three operative clauses given a state (open) with the same named gap.

Evidence is clear that Congress repealed the code-approval and enforcement provisions on 1935-06-14 and set Title I to end 1936-04-01, but the rules bar inferring an ending from a general statute not naming the order. A class ruling for NRA code approvals is needed.

propositions.claim: A GPO slip printing of the order numbered 6313 is held.
The order adopts the Administrator's report, recommendations and findings, under NIRA Title I.
propositions.quote: pursuant to the authority vested in me by title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, approved June 16, 1933, and otherwise, do adopt and approve the report, recommendations and findings

propositions.claim: The order approves the code, subject to one condition.
propositions.quote: do order that the said code of fair competition be and is hereby approved, subject to the following condition

propositions.claim: The condition requires article IV of the code to be eliminated.
propositions.quote: such interpretation should not be incorporated in codes of fair competition. Therefore, article IV must be eliminated.

propositions.claim: Candidate ending: the joint resolution of June 14, 1935 repealed the Title I provisions for presidential approval and enforcement of codes. It does not name EO 6313.
propositions.quote: All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed

propositions.claim: Candidate ending: the same resolution reset the termination date in NIRA Title I sec. 2(c) to April 1, 1936.
propositions.quote: striking out "at the expiration of two years after the date of enactment of this Act" and inserting in lieu thereof "on April 1, 1936"

propositions.claim: The order's own text sets no expiry date or terminating event; the slice lists no later instrument naming it and no current-law citation.
propositions.quote: be and is hereby approved, subject to the following condition

review.conclusion_reason: OPEN is supported by the unexamined approved code's possible duration provisions and the absence of a qualifying ending or positive current source in the checked evidence. The general repeal cannot establish an ending under the supplied rules. Formal status is supportable only as no express ending found in this limited evidence, not an exhaustive finding.
missed_evidence: The held Mabillon printing says 'do adopt and approve the report, recommendations and findings of the Administrator'. This adoption is performed by the order itself and supports treating clause 1 as spent on issue under rule (c), dated October 3, 1933 in the held Photius printing. Leaving that clause open prevents upholding the complete clause-state assessment required for T4.
review.stop_code_verdict: wrong (WEB fits the remaining code-duration evidence gap). NEEDS_RULING is unnecessary: the supplied rules already prohibit inferring an ending from a general statute that does not name the order. The slice's nra_code_approval/swept classification is only a lead, not an exception. Read the approved code at the already identified NRA Codes volume I, page 541, to investigate an own-terms ending.

verdicts.reason: Held Mabillon printing contains [No. 6313] and the 1933 U.S. Government Printing Office imprint.
Held printing expressly invokes NIRA Title I and adopts and approves the Administrator's report, recommendations and findings.
Held printing approves the code subject to the following condition and lists one condition.
Held printing expressly states: 'Therefore, article IV must be eliminated.'
The cited official PDF, 49 Stat. 375, chapter 246, section 2, contains the quoted repeal and June 14, 1935 approval date. It does not name EO 6313; candidate treatment is appropriate.
Section 1 of chapter 246 in the cited PDF makes precisely the quoted substitution in NIRA section 2(c).

The complete held Photius text contains no express expiry date or terminating event. The supplied slice has no later naming instrument or current-law citation. This does not establish absence beyond the slice.
